 • Haloperidol (Haldol®)

 • Lumateperone (Caplyta®)

*URL:* https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/schizoaffective-disorder/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20354509  
*Published Time:* Thu, 13 Mar 2025 04:28:00 GMT  

**Evidence**  
- *Treatment overview:* “People with schizoaffective disorder generally respond best to medicines along with talk therapy and life skills training.”  
- *Medicines – antipsychotics:* “Antipsychotics. Paliperidone (Invega) is the only medicine that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved specifically to treat schizoaffective disorder. But healthcare professionals often prescribe other antipsychotic drugs…”.  
- *Medicines – mood‑stabilizing:* “Mood‑stabilizing medicine. When the schizoaffective disorder is the bipolar type, mood stabilizers can help level out the mania highs and depression lows.”  
- *Medicines – antidepressants:* “Antidepressants. When depression is the underlying mood disorder, antidepressants can help manage feelings of sadness and hopelessness or trouble sleeping and focusing.”  
- *Talk therapy:* “Talk therapy — also called psychotherapy — may help.”  
  - *Individual therapy:* “Individual therapy.”  
  - *Family or group therapy:* “Family or group therapy.”  
- *Life skills training:* “Life skills training can ease isolation and make quality of life better.”  
  - *Social skills training:* “Social skills training.”  
  - *Work rehabilitation and supported work:* “Work rehabilitation and supported work.”  
- *Hospital stay:* “During crisis periods or times of severe symptoms, people with schizoaffective disorder may need to stay in a hospital…”  
- *Electroconvulsive therapy:* “For adults with schizoaffective disorder who do not respond to talk therapy or medicines, healthcare professionals may suggest electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)…”

**Coverage**  
- **Entities (treatment methods) listed:**

### Page note: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/schizophrenia/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20354449
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page**  
*Title:* Schizophrenia – Diagnosis and treatment  
*URL:* https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/schizophrenia/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20354449  

**Evidence**  
- *Medicines* – “Medicines are the main schizophrenia treatment. Antipsychotic medicines are the most prescribed drugs.”  
- *Other medicines* – “Other medicines also may help, such as antidepressants, mood stabilizers or antianxiety drugs.”  
- *Long‑acting injectable antipsychotics* – “Some antipsychotics may be given as a long‑acting shot… Common medicines that are available as shots include: Aripiprazole (Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii, Aristada), Fluphenazine decanoate, Haloperidol decanoate, Paliperidone (Invega Sustenna, Invega Trinza, Invega Hafyera), Risperidone (Risperdal Consta, Perseris, others).”  
- *Psychosocial interventions* – “...psychological and social or psychosocial treatments, including: Individual therapy (talk therapy, psychotherapy), Social skills training, Family therapy, Vocational rehabilitation and supported employment.”  
- *Hospital stay* – “During crisis periods or times of severe symptoms, people may need to stay in a hospital for their safety.”  
- *Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)* – “Healthcare professionals may consider electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for adults with schizophrenia who don't respond to drug therapy. … small electric currents are passed through the brain, causing a therapeutic seizure that lasts 1 to 2 minutes.”

**Coverage**  
- **Entity**: schizophrenia  
- **Treatment methods listed**: medicines (antipsychotics, antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antianxiety drugs), long‑acting injectable antipsychotics, psychosocial interventions (individual therapy, social skills training, family therapy, vocational rehabilitation & supported employment), hospital stay, electroconvulsive therapy.  
- The list is complete for the scope of this page (all treatment methods mentioned).

- Treatment methods for *schizoaffective disorder* (not mentioned on this page).
